rows.question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
rows.answer:
Michael Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
Before launch, the tank's heaters were run on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The fire's cause was the tank's thermostatic switches, which the board's report calls a serious oversight shared by all parties. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The switches were built for 28 volts, but the heater specification was revised to 65 volts in 1965 and the switches were not changed. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The swap came from his exposure: "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)" [[rubella-crew-swap]].

The swap brought in Jack Swigert, who replaced Ken Mattingly. The note's description reads "Backup pilot who replaced Ken Mattingly as Apollo 13 command module pilot one day before launch" [[jack-swigert]] description: "Backup [unverified] pilot who replaced Ken Mattingly as Apollo 13 command module pilot one day before launch".

Swigert later won election to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office. "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)" [[jack-swigert]].

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?

The crew built it from instructions relayed by radio. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The brain does not give the build steps or the order of assembly, so I can't say more about how the adapter was put together.

The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)".

The tank's switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)". rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Here are the 1970 dates the brain records for Apollo 13, in order:

1. **6 April 1970:** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

2. **10 April 1970:** The crew swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference. Jack Swigert replaced Ken Mattingly as command module pilot. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)" [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

3. **11 April 1970:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

4. **13 April 1970:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded, about 56 hours into the flight. The mission goal changed from a lunar landing to a safe return to Earth. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

5. **17 April 1970:** The crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

6. **June 1970:** The Apollo 13 Review Board report was published. Its chair, Edgar Cortright, was director of NASA Langley at the time. The board traced the explosion to a fire in oxygen tank No. 2 started electrically. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The brain gives only the month for the report, so no exact day can be stated.
